requirements.requirement: Persistently disable ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects) for IPv4 on node1, across all relevant interfaces (all/default/eth0/lo)
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 on all/default (cmd-f73b43cfd8d04edb). A sysctl.d config file was created and applied (cmd-3484d4bb6ba44754, cmd-3bf2cb1f4c0748d7). Executor discovered eth0 retained accept_redirects=1 due to per-interface override and corrected it (cmd-0620604a08df4e78, cmd-ae2f764a4b014e52, cmd-7189c69bd3034300, cmd-f53fc054af8e4a35). A reboot was performed with boot_id changing from 15443601... to 08f9094d... (cmd-7d59ce384875426e, cmd-11bd32ac18064383, cmd-a3e1b5b7e51946ff, cmd-cef12b9f30134df6), after which lo.accept_redirects was found reverted to 1 (cmd-d229352da94249b7) and fixed/persisted (cmd-68873b76785441ed). A second reboot (boot_id changed to 4b9f3de9..., cmd-773340a45cdb4d1c, cmd-b3253b41cdab42e9, cmd-531f7f98fea848ca/cmd-94adb4d101284f62, cmd-7eeeacc3cb3341e4) confirmed all/default/eth0/lo accept_redirects read 0 post-restart (cmd-932ca9a6343141dd). This is a direct pre-restart baseline, bounded disruption, and post-restart recovered-state verification.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed IPv4 packets on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 on all/default (cmd-f73b43cfd8d04edb), but the executor still made the setting explicit and persistent via the sysctl.d file (cmd-3484d4bb6ba44754, cmd-3bf2cb1f4c0748d7) and verified it across all interfaces (cmd-0620604a08df4e78, cmd-f53fc054af8e4a35). Post-reboot verification after both restarts confirmed accept_source_route=0 for all/default/eth0/lo (cmd-d229352da94249b7, cmd-932ca9a6343141dd), demonstrating persistence across a genuine reboot (boot_id changes captured in req-1 evidence).

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled ICMP redirect acceptance and IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance on node1 via a sysctl.d config file, correctly discovered and fixed per-interface overrides (eth0, then lo after a post-reboot regression), and proved persistence directly by observing boot_id changes across two genuine reboots with settings confirmed at 0 both times for all/default/eth0/lo. Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence including pre-change baseline, bounded disruption (reboot), and recovered state.
limitations: Minor leftover log files (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/reboot2.log, /tmp/sysctl-apply.log) were not cleaned up post-task, though this has no functional impact.

The independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was not separately distinguished from the task's own restart testing, but the two observed reboots with boot_id changes and pre/post state checks satisfy the substance of that protocol for node1.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands were directly tied to the task: writing/appending to the sysctl.d config file, applying with sysctl --system/-w, and two reboots needed to prove persistence (a reasonable and necessary verification step given the task explicitly requires 'persistent' disablement). The two reboots were bounded, low-risk, and directly served the persistence requirement, and the second reboot was needed to correct a regression found in the first (lo interface). Minor residue: reboot.log, reboot2.log, and sysctl-apply.log were left in /tmp (visible in after_executor temporary-files snapshot) from shell output redirection during the reboot and reapply commands (cmd-11bd32ac18064383, cmd-b3253b41cdab42e9, cmd-68873b76785441ed) and were not cleaned up afterward. This is minor, bounded residue with no functional or security impact, so it only lightly reduces the hygiene score.
